text.p: Consolidated Nevada Goldfields Corp said Friday it acquired certain Grupo Real del Monte SA de CV subsidiaries for 52,290,091 common shares.

In a related transaction, Consolidated said, it completed a private placement of 22,493,570 special warrants at a price of C$1.20 to a Canadian underwriting group, raising total proceeds of C$26,992,284.

The company said it issued 26,363,968 shares to the Mexican mining company and 25,926,123 shares to certain Grupo Real shareholders. In addition, Consolidated said, it granted the Mexican company a 12 percent net profits royalty on the acquired subsidiaries up to a maximum of US$5 million.

The company said the four operating mines acquired increase its proven/probable reserves six-fold to 1.2 million gold equivalent ounces of precious metals comprised of 589,000 ounces of gold and 47 million ounces of silver.
Also included are 31 million pounds of copper and four million metric tonnes of barite.
The company said its production is projected to immediately double.

The special warrants are exercisable into separable units, without payment of additional consideration, each unit consisting of one common share and one-half a common share purchase warrant. Each purchase warrant will entitle the holder to buy one common share at an exercise price of C$1.30 for one year.

In connection with the special warrants transaction, Grupo Acerero del Norte SA de CV, Consolidated's controlling shareholder, acquired 3,761,000 special warrants entitling it to 3,761,000 shares and 1,880,500 purchase warrants.
In total, through the acquisition and the special warrants transaction Grupo Acerero has acquired or is entitled to acquire, for investment purposes, 57,931,591 shares.
